# pr-1526: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main ## Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1526 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1526 - **Title**: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1522` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 28 - **Additions**: +2034 - **Deletions**: -2015 - **Created**: 2026-10-10T22:52:16Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T01:13:11Z ## PR Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1526._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

---

### Thread 2 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

Options:
- Make the repo-file check **non-blocking** in the publish job (a `::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), keeping the staged check as the real gate; or
- Move the repo-file check to a non-release surface (Static gates / nightly) so the release train can't die on it.

Either way, this header (and `docs/ci.md`'s matching claim) should reflect reality. `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` currently pins the release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) — update it with whichever direction is chosen.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/publish_staging_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no behavioral test executes `stamp_staged_release.sh` — the ticket's riskiest new script is pinned by string assertions only**

The stamper is the linchpin of gh-1522 (a bad stamp ships `0.0.0-dev` or a malformed changelog to pub.dev), and its riskiest logic — the Python section split, the `## Unreleased` fold, the cap-trim loop, the last-resort single-section fallback — is only `contains`/`indexOf`-pinned here and in `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`. The nightly dry-run would catch a crash, but nothing asserts the staged *content*: e.g. that the generated section actually lands under `## <version>`, that the staged file no longer shows an `## Unreleased` header, that the version stamp is exactly the tag, and that an over-cap staged file trims oldest-first keeping the fresh section.

This file already has the fixture harness for it (temp dir + `Process.runSync('bash', [stamp_staged_release.sh, …])`, same as `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` exercises `check_changelog_size.sh` behaviorally). A small behavioral group — stamp a fixture stage, assert pubspec + changelog bytes, over-cap trim, missing-version-line loud fail — would close the gap. (Also worth one case: a repo CHANGELOG that already carries a curated `## <version>` section for the same version — today the staged file would show that section twice, since the stamper prepends the generated one and keeps the existing one.)

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: generated changelog section is missing blank lines — raw output runs sections together**

`new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"` produces (verified against a fixture run):

```markdown
## 1.0.550
- something pending
## 1.0.549

- old entry
```

No blank line after the section header, and none between the fresh section and the next `## ` — the published pub.dev changelog renders it acceptably, but the raw markdown is scruffy and inconsistent with the hand-curated sections. Consider `new = f"\n## {version}\n\n{section}\n\n"` (or `.strip()` the section and re-join with explicit blank lines) so the stamped file matches the repo's existing formatting convention.

---

### Thread 5 — `scripts/auto_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: coalesce age reads the tagged commit's date, not the tag's tagger date**

`git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"` (a few lines above, at line 53 — the surrounding block is unchanged by this PR so it can't be anchored directly) dereferences the annotated tag to the commit, so `tag_age` measures the committer date of origin/main's tip *at tag time* — not when the tag was cut. The two diverge whenever commits sat pending on main before the cron/dispatch cut the tag (the common catch-up path this file exists for): a tag cut 10 minutes ago can read hours old, so a new push would not be coalesced even though the 2h window since the *release* hasn't elapsed — the extra releases are exactly what this guard (and the pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to prevent. Use the tag object date instead:

```bash
tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag") ))
```

---

### Thread 6 — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: step name no longer describes what it verifies**

`Verify tag matches pubspec version` now does the inverse of its name — it checks that the committed pubspec is still the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder and no longer compares the tag to the pubspec at all (the binaries-job twin was already renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder`). The stale name will mislead the next person reading a failed run. Rename to match the twin.

---

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The tag-only release redesign is solid and the docs/tests were reworked thoroughly, but CI is red: both new E1 race tests fail on `test-core` (and `hostile-env`) because the rewritten race hook dropped the inline git identity the retired hook carried — the racer's annotated tag fails on runners without a global git identity, so the race never happens.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 The race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needs `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` (restores the pre-gh-1522 pattern); reproduced locally with a scrubbed git env — details in the inline thread.
- ⚠️ The publish job still hard-fails on an over-cap **repo** CHANGELOG.md, contradicting gh-1522's core promise that the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release (the staged-side trim already fully protects the upload).
- 💡 Stamper lacks a behavioral test; generated changelog sections run t…

# pr-1526: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main ## Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```

### Thread 1 — `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

---

### Thread 2 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

Options:
- Make the repo-file check **non-blocking** in the publish job (a `::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), keeping the staged check as the real gate; or
- Move the repo-file check to a non-release surface (Static gates / nightly) so the release train can't die on it.

Either way, this header (and `docs/ci.md`'s matching claim) should reflect reality. `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` currently pins the release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) — update it with whichever direction is chosen.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no behavioral test executes `stamp_staged_release.sh` — the ticket's riskiest new script is pinned by string assertions only**

The stamper is the linchpin of gh-1522 (a bad stamp ships `0.0.0-dev` or a malformed changelog to pub.dev), and its riskiest logic — the Python section split, the `## Unreleased` fold, the cap-trim loop, the last-resort single-section fallback — is only `contains`/`indexOf`-pinned here and in `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`. The nightly dry-run would catch a crash, but nothing asserts the staged *content*: e.g. that the generated section actually lands under `## <version>`, that the staged file no longer shows an `## Unreleased` header, that the version stamp is exactly the tag, and that an over-cap staged file trims oldest-first keeping the fresh section.

This file already has the fixture harness for it (temp dir + `Process.runSync('bash', [stamp_staged_release.sh, …])`, same as `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` exercises `check_changelog_size.sh` behaviorally). A small behavioral group — stamp a fixture stage, assert pubspec + changelog bytes, over-cap trim, missing-version-line loud fail — would close the gap. ### Thread 4 — `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: generated changelog section is missing blank lines — raw output runs sections together**

`new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"` produces (verified against a fixture run):

```markdown
## 1.0.550
- something pending
## 1.0.549

- old entry
```

No blank line after the section header, and none between the fresh section and the next `## ` — the published pub.dev changelog renders it acceptably, but the raw markdown is scruffy and inconsistent with the hand-curated sections. Consider `new = f"\n## {version}\n\n{section}\n\n"` (or `.strip()` the section and re-join with explicit blank lines) so the stamped file matches the repo's existing formatting convention.

# pr-1526: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main ## Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1526 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1526 - **Title**: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1522` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 28 - **Additions**: +2034 - **Deletions**: -2015 - **Created**: 2026-10-10T22:52:16Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T01:13:11Z ## PR Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1526._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

---

### Thread 2 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

Options:
- Make the repo-file check **non-blocking** in the publish job (a `::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), keeping the staged check as the real gate; or
- Move the repo-file check to a non-release surface (Static gates / nightly) so the release train can't die on it.

Either way, this header (and `docs/ci.md`'s matching claim) should reflect reality. `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` currently pins the release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) — update it with whichever direction is chosen.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/publish_staging_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no behavioral test executes `stamp_staged_release.sh` — the ticket's riskiest new script is pinned by string assertions only**

The stamper is the linchpin of gh-1522 (a bad stamp ships `0.0.0-dev` or a malformed changelog to pub.dev), and its riskiest logic — the Python section split, the `## Unreleased` fold, the cap-trim loop, the last-resort single-section fallback — is only `contains`/`indexOf`-pinned here and in `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`. The nightly dry-run would catch a crash, but nothing asserts the staged *content*: e.g. that the generated section actually lands under `## <version>`, that the staged file no longer shows an `## Unreleased` header, that the version stamp is exactly the tag, and that an over-cap staged file trims oldest-first keeping the fresh section.

This file already has the fixture harness for it (temp dir + `Process.runSync('bash', [stamp_staged_release.sh, …])`, same as `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` exercises `check_changelog_size.sh` behaviorally). A small behavioral group — stamp a fixture stage, assert pubspec + changelog bytes, over-cap trim, missing-version-line loud fail — would close the gap. (Also worth one case: a repo CHANGELOG that already carries a curated `## <version>` section for the same version — today the staged file would show that section twice, since the stamper prepends the generated one and keeps the existing one.)

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: generated changelog section is missing blank lines — raw output runs sections together**

`new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"` produces (verified against a fixture run):

```markdown
## 1.0.550
- something pending
## 1.0.549

- old entry
```

No blank line after the section header, and none between the fresh section and the next `## ` — the published pub.dev changelog renders it acceptably, but the raw markdown is scruffy and inconsistent with the hand-curated sections. Consider `new = f"\n## {version}\n\n{section}\n\n"` (or `.strip()` the section and re-join with explicit blank lines) so the stamped file matches the repo's existing formatting convention.

---

### Thread 5 — `scripts/auto_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: coalesce age reads the tagged commit's date, not the tag's tagger date**

`git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"` (a few lines above, at line 53 — the surrounding block is unchanged by this PR so it can't be anchored directly) dereferences the annotated tag to the commit, so `tag_age` measures the committer date of origin/main's tip *at tag time* — not when the tag was cut. The two diverge whenever commits sat pending on main before the cron/dispatch cut the tag (the common catch-up path this file exists for): a tag cut 10 minutes ago can read hours old, so a new push would not be coalesced even though the 2h window since the *release* hasn't elapsed — the extra releases are exactly what this guard (and the pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to prevent. Use the tag object date instead:

```bash
tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag") ))
```

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: step name no longer describes what it verifies**

`Verify tag matches pubspec version` now does the inverse of its name — it checks that the committed pubspec is still the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder and no longer compares the tag to the pubspec at all (the binaries-job twin was already renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder`). The stale name will mislead the next person reading a failed run. Rename to match the twin.

# pr-1526: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main ## Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1526 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1526 - **Title**: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1522` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 28 - **Additions**: +2034 - **Deletions**: -2015 - **Created**: 2026-10-10T22:52:16Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T01:13:11Z ## PR Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1526._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

---

### Thread 2 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

Options:
- Make the repo-file check **non-blocking** in the publish job (a `::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), keeping the staged check as the real gate; or
- Move the repo-file check to a non-release surface (Static gates / nightly) so the release train can't die on it.

Either way, this header (and `docs/ci.md`'s matching claim) should reflect reality. `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` currently pins the release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) — update it with whichever direction is chosen.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/publish_staging_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no behavioral test executes `stamp_staged_release.sh` — the ticket's riskiest new script is pinned by string assertions only**

The stamper is the linchpin of gh-1522 (a bad stamp ships `0.0.0-dev` or a malformed changelog to pub.dev), and its riskiest logic — the Python section split, the `## Unreleased` fold, the cap-trim loop, the last-resort single-section fallback — is only `contains`/`indexOf`-pinned here and in `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`. The nightly dry-run would catch a crash, but nothing asserts the staged *content*: e.g. that the generated section actually lands under `## <version>`, that the staged file no longer shows an `## Unreleased` header, that the version stamp is exactly the tag, and that an over-cap staged file trims oldest-first keeping the fresh section.

This file already has the fixture harness for it (temp dir + `Process.runSync('bash', [stamp_staged_release.sh, …])`, same as `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` exercises `check_changelog_size.sh` behaviorally). A small behavioral group — stamp a fixture stage, assert pubspec + changelog bytes, over-cap trim, missing-version-line loud fail — would close the gap. (Also worth one case: a repo CHANGELOG that already carries a curated `## <version>` section for the same version — today the staged file would show that section twice, since the stamper prepends the generated one and keeps the existing one.)

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: generated changelog section is missing blank lines — raw output runs sections together**

`new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"` produces (verified against a fixture run):

```markdown
## 1.0.550
- something pending
## 1.0.549

- old entry
```

No blank line after the section header, and none between the fresh section and the next `## ` — the published pub.dev changelog renders it acceptably, but the raw markdown is scruffy and inconsistent with the hand-curated sections. Consider `new = f"\n## {version}\n\n{section}\n\n"` (or `.strip()` the section and re-join with explicit blank lines) so the stamped file matches the repo's existing formatting convention.

---

### Thread 5 — `scripts/auto_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: coalesce age reads the tagged commit's date, not the tag's tagger date**

`git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag"` (a few lines above, at line 53 — the surrounding block is unchanged by this PR so it can't be anchored directly) dereferences the annotated tag to the commit, so `tag_age` measures the committer date of origin/main's tip *at tag time* — not when the tag was cut. The two diverge whenever commits sat pending on main before the cron/dispatch cut the tag (the common catch-up path this file exists for): a tag cut 10 minutes ago can read hours old, so a new push would not be coalesced even though the 2h window since the *release* hasn't elapsed — the extra releases are exactly what this guard (and the pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to prevent. Use the tag object date instead:

```bash
tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag") ))
```

---

### Thread 6 — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: step name no longer describes what it verifies**

`Verify tag matches pubspec version` now does the inverse of its name — it checks that the committed pubspec is still the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder and no longer compares the tag to the pubspec at all (the binaries-job twin was already renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder`). The stale name will mislead the next person reading a failed run. Rename to match the twin.

---

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The tag-only release redesign is solid and the docs/tests were reworked thoroughly, but CI is red: both new E1 race tests fail on `test-core` (and `hostile-env`) because the rewritten race hook dropped the inline git identity the retired hook carried — the racer's annotated tag fails on runners without a global git identity, so the race never happens.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 The race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needs `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` (restores the pre-gh-1522 pattern); reproduced locally with a scrubbed git env — details in the inline thread.
- ⚠️ The publish job still hard-fails on an over-cap **repo** CHANGELOG.md, contradicting gh-1522's core promise that the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release (the staged-side trim already fully protects the upload).
- 💡 Stamper lacks a behavioral test; generated changelog sections run t…

# pr-1526: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main ## Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1526._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

---

### Thread 2 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

# pr-1526: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main ## Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1526 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1526 - **Title**: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1522` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 28 - **Additions**: +2034 - **Deletions**: -2015 - **Created**: 2026-10-10T22:52:16Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T01:13:11Z ## PR Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1526._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

---

### Thread 2 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

Options:
- Make the repo-file check **non-blocking** in the publish job (a `::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), keeping the staged check as the real gate; or
- Move the repo-file check to a non-release surface (Static gates / nightly) so the release train can't die on it.

Either way, this header (and `docs/ci.md`'s matching claim) should reflect reality. `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` currently pins the release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) — update it with whichever direction is chosen.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/publish_staging_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no behavioral test executes `stamp_staged_release.sh` — the ticket's riskiest new script is pinned by string assertions only**

The stamper is the linchpin of gh-1522 (a bad stamp ships `0.0.0-dev` or a malformed changelog to pub.dev), and its riskiest logic — the Python section split, the `## Unreleased` fold, the cap-trim loop, the last-resort single-section fallback — is only `contains`/`indexOf`-pinned here and in `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`. The nightly dry-run would catch a crash, but nothing asserts the staged *content*: e.g. that the generated section actually lands under `## <version>`, that the staged file no longer shows an `## Unreleased` header, that the version stamp is exactly the tag, and that an over-cap staged file trims oldest-first keeping the fresh section.

This file already has the fixture harness for it (temp dir + `Process.runSync('bash', [stamp_staged_release.sh, …])`, same as `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` exercises `check_changelog_size.sh` behaviorally). A small behavioral group — stamp a fixture stage, assert pubspec + changelog bytes, over-cap trim, missing-version-line loud fail — would close the gap. (Also worth one case: a repo CHANGELOG that already carries a curated `## <version>` section for the same version — today the staged file would show that section twice, since the stamper prepends the generated one and keeps the existing one.)

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`

# pr-1526: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main ## Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```
Release flow after this change ```mermaid flowchart TD AR[auto_release.sh
tag-only] -->|annotated tag vX.Y.Z on origin/main| GH[gh release create] PUSH[v* tag push] --> PUB[ci.yml publish] PUB --> STAGE[stage_publish_package.sh + stamp_staged_release.sh] STAGE --> PUBLISH[dart pub publish --force] PUB --> BIN[binaries job
version from GITHUB_REF_NAME] PUB --> VERIFY[verify_pubdev_release.sh
served vs latest remote tag] PLAN[daily_plan.sh] -->|re-arm while served < latest tag| AR ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1526 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1526 - **Title**: gh-1522 [GOAL] Tag-sourced versions: retire release-bot file bumps — CI stamps pubspec/CHANGELOG at publish time, flutter builds take --build-name, zero release commits to main - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1522` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 28 - **Additions**: +2034 - **Deletions**: -2015 - **Created**: 2026-10-10T22:52:16Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T01:13:11Z ## PR Description Closes #1522 ## What changed Retired the release-bot pubspec/CHANGELOG/lockfile bump on main: `auto_release.sh` now only cuts the next `vX.Y.Z` annotated tag on `origin/main` (with race-retry push and one `gh release create`), and every artifact gets its version at build time from the tag. Placeholder `version: 0.0.0-dev` lives in both pubspecs permanently; `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` stamps the staged publish tree (pubspec + curated changelog section, folding `## Unreleased`, with the 256 KiB cap enforced at stage time). `tag_release.sh`, the `release-tag` job, and the bump-scan logic in `verify_pubdev_release.sh`/`daily_plan.sh` are gone; plan/verify now compare pub.dev against the latest remote tag. ## Key decisions - **One release-create owner**: `auto_release.sh` owns the single `gh release create`; the old tag-leg create was deleted (AC3 inverted). - **Staged stamp, not committed bumps**: publish (`ci.yml`), nightly dry-run, and binaries all derive the version from the git tag (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` / `git describe`), so the pubspec in the repo never needs a bump commit again. - **Changelog source of truth**: staged changelog prefers a curated `## ` section, then folds the `## Unreleased` body, then falls back to conventional commits (`release_notes.sh`); `check_changelog_size.sh` gained a `--max-bytes` override so the gate measures the stamped file. - **Fastlane/store builds**: `store_pubspec_version` now prefers `ENV["BUILD_NAME"]` (the `version` job's latest-tag+1 derivation stays the store flow); Android `build_release` passes `--build-name` when set. - **Lockfile pin stability**: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` now pins `0.0.0-dev` forever — `check_lockfiles.sh` gh-1303 equality holds with no further regen. - Guard wiring pinned by tests: `workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test` (blobless full-history checkout) and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test` (enforce-lockfile rationale) updated to the tag-only flow. ## How to verify ```bash dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart # full suite (run during this change): dart test --exclude-tags integration # 10183 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1526._

> ℹ️ **2 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI is red — the race hook's annotated tag in the racer clone fails without an ambient git identity**

The `test-core` leg fails (`Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (test-core)`) on both new E1 tests, and `hostile-env` fails on the same two:

- `E1 race — a tag that appeared mid-run rejects the push …` — expected `Tag push raced`, got `Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496`
- `E1 exhaustion — a tag race on every attempt exits 1 …` — expected exit 1, got 0

Root cause: the racer clone gets **no git identity**, and the rewritten hook creates an *annotated* tag (`git tag -a`), which requires one. On hosts without a global `user.name`/`user.email` (GitHub runners, the hostile-env leg) the hook's `git tag -a` dies with `fatal: empty ident name … not allowed` → the racer never pre-pushes the tag → the script's own push succeeds → no race, tests fail. The retired main-push hook this replaces carried the identity inline — `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` — and the rewrite dropped it. I reproduced the exact CI failure locally with `HOME=<empty> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`.

Fix — restore the inline identity on the racer's tag command (the seed clone's `git config` does not leak into the racer):

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t \
  -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(Setting `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` in `baseEnv` would work too, but the inline `-c` matches the fixture's established pattern.)

---

### Thread 2 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the repo-file changelog gate still blocks releases — this claim (and the ticket's core promise) is not delivered**

This sentence says the in-repo CHANGELOG's size "can never block a release again" — but the `publish` job still runs `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` on the **repo file** as a hard pre-staging gate (ci.yml, "Publish gate" step): an over-cap repo CHANGELOG fails the whole publish job, exactly the #1452 class gh-1522 was opened to retire. The ticket is explicit: *"even if it inflates, the published artifact's changelog is generated — the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release."*

The staged-side protection is already complete without the repo-file gate: `stamp_staged_release.sh` trims the oldest staged sections to fit, re-measures with `check_changelog_size.sh`, and has a last-resort single-section fallback before failing loud — the uploaded artifact can never trip the server cap. (Note the repo file isn't even what pub packs; the staged tree is.)

Options:
- Make the repo-file check **non-blocking** in the publish job (a `::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), keeping the staged check as the real gate; or
- Move the repo-file check to a non-release surface (Static gates / nightly) so the release train can't die on it.

Either way, this header (and `docs/ci.md`'s matching claim) should reflect reality. `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` currently pins the release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) — update it with whichever direction is chosen.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/publish_staging_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no behavioral test executes `stamp_staged_release.sh` — the ticket's riskiest new script is pinned by string assertions only**

The stamper is the linchpin of gh-1522 (a bad stamp ships `0.0.0-dev` or a malformed changelog to pub.dev), and its riskiest logic — the Python section split, the `## Unreleased` fold, the cap-trim loop, the last-resort single-section fallback — is only `contains`/`indexOf`-pinned here and in `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`. The nightly dry-run would catch a crash, but nothing asserts the staged *content*: e.g. that the generated section actually lands under `## <version>`, that the staged file no longer shows an `## Unreleased` header, that the version stamp is exactly the tag, and that an over-cap staged file trims oldest-first keeping the fresh section.

This file already has the fixture harness for it (temp dir + `Process.runSync('bash', [stamp_staged_release.sh, …])`, same as `changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` exercises `check_changelog_size.sh` behaviorally). A small behavioral group — stamp a fixture stage, assert pubspec + changelog bytes, over-cap trim, missing-version-line loud fail — would close the gap. (Also worth one case: a repo CHANGELOG that already carries a curated `## <version>` section for the same version — today the staged file would show that section twice, since the stamper prepends the generated one and keeps the existing one.)

---

### Thread 4 — `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: generated changelog section is missing blank lines — raw output runs sections together**

`new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"` produces (verified against a fixture run):

```markdown
## 1.0.550
- something pending
## 1.0.549

- old entry
