tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generates an image from a text prompt. Returns a path to the saved image file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1024x1024"), quality (optional).

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generates a video from a text prompt. Returns a path to the saved MP4 file. Arguments: prompt (required), size (optional, e.g. "1920x1080"), quality (optional).

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Check the status of spawned subagents. Without an id, lists ALL subagents with their current state, token usage, and last activity. With an id, shows that subagent in detail.

tools.name: task_observe
tools.description: Read the recent message history of a subagent. Useful to inspect what a child discovered or decided before following up.

tools.name: task_send
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running child receives it in its inbox at the next turn boundary; an idle (waiting for input) or completed child is resumed in its SAME session with the message. The resume wait is capped (1s): a child that does not respond in time reports the message queued and keeps waking in the background (check task_status). Failed children are continued with task_resume instead. Remote a2a:<name> children cannot be steered or resumed — they have no local session or inbox; follow up with a new task item.

tools.name: task_resume
tools.description: Resume a FAILED subagent, continuing the SAME session: the run appends to the existing JSONL transcript, keeps the same mailbox id and display name, and never mints a cloned "name-2" session. Use this after transient failures (provider quota, network). Steering running/idle/completed children is task_send; respawning a fresh agent is task (the new child links supersedes).

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Abort a running background subagent job by id (see task_status for ids). The child agent is cancelled; already-settled jobs report their state instead.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

tools.name: agent_message
tools.description: Send a message to another agent: a SIBLING subagent id, "main" for the parent orchestrator (for a final answer prefer reply), an absolute mailbox "<sessionId>/main" to reach another Fa instance sharing this session repo, or "name@machine" to reach a session on another machine (delivered through the A2A gateway; the remote machine must be configured under a2a.servers). A session display NAME from agent_directory works too: "goal_builder" or "goal_builder/main" resolve to that session's live mailbox. The recipient sees the message in its inbox on its next turn; completed siblings are resumed. Unknown ids and full queues are rejected.

tools.name: agent_directory
tools.description: List the agent mailboxes in the messaging fabric that are worth talking to: LIVE mailboxes (registration-backed presence or recent activity), any mailbox holding pending mail, your subagents, and your own address (marked). Each entry shows its session display NAME when known, a short mailbox id, the pending message count, presence ("live" / "busy (run in progress, accepts mail)" / "offline"), the last-activity time for offline entries, and the working directory (home shortened to ~). Declared capabilities render as sub-lines. Stale mailboxes are hidden — pass all: true to list those too (that also shows FULL mailbox ids; the default view truncates them to save tokens). Address a mailbox by its session name via agent_message ("goal_builder", "goal_builder/main", or "name@machine" — a peer on another machine is reachable through the A2A gateway when an a2a.servers entry exists for it); asleep targets are woken with a headless run automatically.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Run subagents in parallel by passing multiple items in a single `tasks[]` batch. Execution blocks until every item finishes unless `background` is true — then you receive job ids immediately and results deliver as jobs settle.

# Task Design
- **Agent typing:** Pick each item's `agent` type. Read-only research MUST use `agent: "explore"`. Use the default worker only when no specialist fits.
- **No overhead:** Each `task` MUST instruct its subagent to skip formatters, linters, and project-wide test suites. Run those once at the end.
- **One pass:** Prefer subagents that investigate AND edit in one pass; spin a read-only `explore` only when the affected files are genuinely unknown.

# Inputs
- `context`: Shared project state, constraints, and contracts. Applies to the entire batch; do not duplicate this background into individual tasks.
- `tasks[]`: Array of subagents to spawn.
  - `name`: A stable identifier (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`), used to address the agent (`agent://` urls, job ids). Uniquified per session; generated from the agent type if omitted.
  - `agent`: The agent type running this item. Omitting it gives you the general-purpose worker (`task`) — NEVER pass that name explicitly. Only omit it after checking the agent list below and finding no specialist that fits.
  - `task`: Complete, self-contained instructions. One-liners or missing acceptance criteria are PROHIBITED.
  - `outputSchema`: Invocation-specific JSON Schema. The subagent's final message must then be a JSON document satisfying it; invalid output gets ONE fix retry, then the item fails.
- `background`: Run items as background jobs (default: host configuration). Blocking calls return every item's output in the result.

# Communication
Subagents start blank — no conversation history. Put everything they need into `context` (shared) and `task` (per item). After spawn, the family stays connected:
- `task_send {id, message}`: steer a running child, answer a waiting (idle) one, or RESUME a completed one with follow-up work.
- `task_resume {id, message?}`: continue a FAILED child in its SAME session — same id, same transcript, same mailbox, never a cloned `name-2` session. Use it after transient failures (provider quota, network); `task_send` is for running/idle/completed children, a fresh `task` for a clean restart (the new child links `supersedes`).
- `task_status` / `task_observe`: inspect the family at any time — status, tokens, and the child's recent transcript.
- Children can `reply` (their explicit answer to you) and `agent_message` (sibling↔sibling hand-offs) — a child that finishes without replying surfaces a `completed_without_reply` notice with its final text preview.
- Completed subagents stay addressable: send them more work instead of re-spawning duplicates.
- Remote `a2a:<name>` children cannot be steered, resumed, or observed — they have no local session. Follow up with a new task item against the same `a2a:<name>` agent.

# Waiting is idle, not blocked
- Long-running children (test suites, builds, research): spawn them with `background: true` and END YOUR TURN right after spawning. Completions and inbox mail wake you automatically, and each result arrives as a message — waiting is an idle state, never a blocked turn.
- NEVER park your turn waiting on children (foreground watch loops, blocking re-polls, sleep-style watchers). A parked turn is unreachable: owner messages queue behind it for as long as the wedge lasts.
- If a blocking call is still running when a user message arrives, the call soft-yields to background — do not re-block afterwards; finish the reply and end the turn.

# Format Contracts
`context` format:
# Goal         ← what the batch accomplishes
# Constraints  ← rules and session decisions
# Contract     ← shared interfaces

`task` format:
# Target       ← exact files and symbols; explicit non-goals
# Change       ← step-by-step add/remove/rename; APIs and patterns
# Acceptance   ← observable result; no project-wide commands

# Results
Each item's full output is addressable as `agent://<id>`. For items with an `outputSchema`, the stored output IS the validated JSON object, so typed fields are addressable as `agent://<id>/<dot.path>` (e.g. `agent://Explore/findings.0.path`).

# Available Agents
### task
General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
### explore (READ-ONLY)
Read-only codebase research: rapid analysis, pattern searches, and compressed findings for handoff (uses the smol model role when configured)
### review (READ-ONLY)
Read-only code review specialist for quality and security analysis (uses the slow model role when configured)
### plan (READ-ONLY)
Read-only planning specialist that produces implementation plans without editing code

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description:
Creates a context checkpoint before exploratory work so you can later rewind and keep only a concise report.

Use this when you need to investigate with many intermediate tool calls (read/grep/glob/etc.) and want to minimize context cost afterward.

Rules:
- You MUST call `rewind` before finishing after starting a checkpoint.
- You NEVER call `checkpoint` while another checkpoint is active in the
  same turn. A checkpoint never spans user turns: if one is left unrewound
  when the turn ends, the next `checkpoint` call auto-closes it (the tool
  result names the closed checkpoint) and proceeds.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Perform exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After rewind, intermediate checkpoint messages are removed from active context and replaced by the report. The dropped history stays in the session tree; nothing is lost.

tools.name: rewind
tools.description:
End an active checkpoint. Rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

Call immediately after `checkpoint`-started investigative work.

Requirements:
- `report` MUST be concise, factual, and actionable.
- Include key findings, decisions, and any unresolved risks.
- AVOID raw scratch logs unless essential.
- You MUST call this before finishing if a checkpoint is active.

Behavior:
- If no checkpoint is active, this tool errors. If the checkpoint already rewound, continue from the retained report instead of retrying.
- On success, the session rewinds, keeps your report as retained context, and closes the checkpoint.
- A successful rewind is final for that checkpoint; repeat calls error.

tools.name: compact_expand
tools.description:
Surface and reopen hidden context segments.

Call with NO arguments to list what is hidden: the index of hidden segments with id, kind, size, and a first-line preview each. Pass `query` to filter and rank that index by keyword — it searches the full hidden content, not just previews, so use it when you know WHAT you need but not the id. Discovery is free: it never consumes the expand budget.

To read a segment back, pass its numeric id or range from a marker as `target` (e.g. `5` or `2-6`). Context markers like `[3:hidden·tool_result·4.2k·"first line…"]` or `[2-6:ckpt·38k→40tok·covers:3,5]` are doors, not gravestones: the underlying records stay on disk.

- Giant segments are paged: pass `page` (1-based) to continue past the first page; each page footer states the exact continue call.
- Expanded content counts toward a per-turn budget; every success states the budget left, and when the budget is exhausted the result says so and resets on the next user turn. Only hidden, checkpoint-covered, or summary-folded records expand — the tool tells you when a record is already visible.
- The session file never changes; an expanded segment may be re-hidden later by compaction.

Prefer a targeted expand over re-reading files when the fact was already in context once, and prefer discovery + query over blind ids.

## Managing segments yourself (tier 2)

Pass `action` with a `target` to manage segments directly, without waiting for pressure:

- `action: "hide"` folds a segment you know is dead weight into its expandable marker immediately — one-line marker stays where the content was, `compact_expand` reopens it any time. Real user turns are never hideable; pair groups hide whole; the most recent turns and pinned segments are rejected with the reason.
- `action: "pin"` shields a segment from every hide/compact path (yours, the judge's, pressure-time LRU re-hide); `action: "unpin"` releases it. Pins render on the marker (`·pinned`) and survive session reload.

Hiding and pinning are session state, not edits: the records stay in the file byte-for-byte.

{"content":"# Rework — PR #1526 (gh-1522 tag-sourced versions)

All 6 open review threads addressed (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 4 SUGGESTION), the merge conflicts with `main` resolved, and every fix landed TDD-style (RED reproduction → fix → GREEN). The three `no-id` machine records (review summary, gh-807 verdict audit, gh-840 rework-consume) carry no thread/reply targets — the verdict record explicitly says "Do not edit or reply" — so they are covered by this top-level comment instead of threaded replies.

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflicts** (`pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): resolved keeping the gh-1522 `0.0.0-dev` placeholder side (main had bumped versions); all three `git add`ed, `git diff --check` clean.
- **CI root cause** (Quality gate, test-core leg): exactly the BLOCKING thread — the rewritten race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needed an inline git identity. Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.
- Skipped nothing: even the suggestion-level threads got code fixes plus behavioral tests.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. Implemented as a single line: a trailing-backslash continuation proved unreliable inside the generated shim (`-C: command not found`).
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, repo-file changelog gate)** — took the reviewer's option A: the publish gate's repo-file check is now **advisory** (`if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` → `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`); the staged re-measure/trim inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` stays the hard pre-upload gate. Aligned `CHANGELOG.md` header, `docs/ci.md`, `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` header, and rewired the guard test (old test pinned the release-blocking wiring).
3. **Thread 3 (stamper behavioral tests)** — new group in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` executing the real script against fixture stages: version stamp bytes, Unreleased fold, over-cap oldest-first trim, loud missing-version fail, and the flagged duplicate-curated-section case (fixed in the stamper: a kept section whose header equals the fresh version is dropped).
4. **Thread 4 (blank lines)** — the generated section is now built as `\n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n` over a normalized preamble, matching the repo's hand-curated markdown convention; pinned behaviorally.
5. **Thread 5 (coalesce age)** — `auto_release.sh` reads `%(taggerdate:unix)` via `git for-each-ref` (commit-date fallback for a hypothetical lightweight tag). New divergent-age fixture test: commit 5h old, tag cut now → coalesces.
6. **Thread 6 (stale step name)** — renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)`, matching the binaries-job twin.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` | merge-conflict resolution — keep the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder |
| `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` | racer-tag inline identity; `commitAgeHours` fixture param; tagger-date coalesce test |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | advisory repo-file changelog check; stale step renamed |
| `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` | header: ci.yml caller documented as advisory |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/ci.md` | claims aligned with the advisory gate reality |
| `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` | advisory-wiring + staged-hard-gate tests replace the old release-blocking pin |
| `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` | blank-line formatting; same-version dedupe; `|| true` so the missing-version loud fail actually speaks |
| `test/publish_staging_test.dart` | behavioral group executing the stamper (6 tests) |
| `scripts/auto_release.sh` | coalesce age from tagger date |

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproductions before every fix**: E1 race tests under empty `HOME` (thread 1); new guard test against the old blocking ci.yml (thread 2); duplicate-section + formatting + missing-version cases (threads 3/4); tagger-date coalesce test against the old commit-date code (thread 5).
- **Targeted suites (all green)**:
  - `dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` — 127 passed
  - `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` — 89 passed
  - hostile-env re-verification: `HOME=<empty>` E1 group — 7 passed
- **Full suite**: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see final comment status (launched after all edits froze).
- `dart analyze` on the three touched test files: no errors (4 pre-existing info-level `curly_braces` lints, untouched). ci.yml re-parsed as valid YAML.
- Deliberately did **not** run `dart format` on the touched test files: the PR's versions were already format-dirty, so a format pass would add unrelated churn; my edits follow the surrounding style.

-  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
+  # The 2h window runs from the RELEASE, not from the commit the tag points
+  # at: commits can sit pending on main for hours before the cron/dispatch
+  # cuts the tag (the common catch-up path), and reading the commit date
+  # would let extra releases through exactly when this guard (and the
+  # pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to stop them (PR #1526 thread 5).

+  # this script, but defensive) falls back to the commit date.
+  tag_ts=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag")
+  [ -n "$tag_ts" ] || tag_ts=$(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag")

{"content":"# Rework — PR #1526 (gh-1522 tag-sourced versions)

All 6 open review threads addressed (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 4 SUGGESTION), the merge conflicts with `main` resolved, and every fix landed TDD-style (RED reproduction → fix → GREEN). The three `no-id` machine records (review summary, gh-807 verdict audit, gh-840 rework-consume) carry no thread/reply targets — the verdict record explicitly says "Do not edit or reply" — so they are covered by this top-level comment instead of threaded replies.

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflicts** (`pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): resolved keeping the gh-1522 `0.0.0-dev` placeholder side (main had bumped versions); all three `git add`ed, `git diff --check` clean.

Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.
- Skipped nothing: even the suggestion-level threads got code fixes plus behavioral tests.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. Implemented as a single line: a trailing-backslash continuation proved unreliable inside the generated shim (`-C: command not found`).
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, repo-file changelog gate)** — took the reviewer's option A: the publish gate's repo-file check is now **advisory** (`if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` → `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`); the staged re-measure/trim inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` stays the hard pre-upload gate. 3. **Thread 3 (stamper behavioral tests)** — new group in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` executing the real script against fixture stages: version stamp bytes, Unreleased fold, over-cap oldest-first trim, loud missing-version fail, and the flagged duplicate-curated-section case (fixed in the stamper: a kept section whose header equals the fresh version is dropped).
4. **Thread 4 (blank lines)** — the generated section is now built as `\n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n` over a normalized preamble, matching the repo's hand-curated markdown convention; pinned behaviorally.
5. **Thread 5 (coalesce age)** — `auto_release.sh` reads `%(taggerdate:unix)` via `git for-each-ref` (commit-date fallback for a hypothetical lightweight tag). New divergent-age fixture test: commit 5h old, tag cut now → coalesces.

index 8ad7c8bca..fecba9bd0 100755
--- a/scripts/auto_release.sh
+++ b/scripts/auto_release.sh
@@ -50,7 +50,16 @@ if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
     echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
     exit 0
   fi
-  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
+  # The 2h window runs from the RELEASE, not from the commit the tag points
+  # at: commits can sit pending on main for hours before the cron/dispatch
+  # cuts the tag (the common catch-up path), and reading the commit date
+  # would let extra releases through exactly when this guard (and the
+  # pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to stop them (PR #1526 thread 5).
+  # Annotated tags carry a tagger date; a lightweight tag (never cut by
+  # this script, but defensive) falls back to the commit date.
+  tag_ts=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag")
+  [ -n "$tag_ts" ] || tag_ts=$(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag")
+  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - tag_ts ))
   if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
     echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
     exit 0

 # here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
-stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}')

+stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}' || true)

The three `no-id` machine records (review summary, gh-807 verdict audit, gh-840 rework-consume) carry no thread/reply targets — the verdict record explicitly says "Do not edit or reply" — so they are covered by this top-level comment instead of threaded replies.

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflicts** (`pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): resolved keeping the gh-1522 `0.0.0-dev` placeholder side (main had bumped versions); all three `git add`ed, `git diff --check` clean.
- **CI root cause** (Quality gate, test-core leg): exactly the BLOCKING thread — the rewritten race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needed an inline git identity. Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.
- Skipped nothing: even the suggestion-level threads got code fixes plus behavioral tests.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. Implemented as a single line: a trailing-backslash continuation proved unreliable inside the generated shim (`-C: command not found`).
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, repo-file changelog gate)** — took the reviewer's option A: the publish gate's repo-file check is now **advisory** (`if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` → `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`); the staged re-measure/trim inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` stays the hard pre-upload gate. Aligned `CHANGELOG.md` header, `docs/ci.md`, `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` header, and rewired the guard test (old test pinned the release-blocking wiring).
3. **Thread 3 (stamper behavioral tests)** — new group in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` executing the real script against fixture stages: version stamp bytes, Unreleased fold, over-cap oldest-first trim, loud missing-version fail, and the flagged duplicate-curated-section case (fixed in the stamper: a kept section whose header equals the fresh version is dropped).
4. **Thread 4 (blank lines)** — the generated section is now built as `\n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n` over a normalized preamble, matching the repo's hand-curated markdown convention; pinned behaviorally.
5. **Thread 5 (coalesce age)** — `auto_release.sh` reads `%(taggerdate:unix)` via `git for-each-ref` (commit-date fallback for a hypothetical lightweight tag). New divergent-age fixture test: commit 5h old, tag cut now → coalesces.
6. **Thread 6 (stale step name)** — renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)`, matching the binaries-job twin.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` | merge-conflict resolution — keep the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder |
| `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` | racer-tag inline identity; `commitAgeHours` fixture param; tagger-date coalesce test |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | advisory repo-file changelog check; stale step renamed |
| `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` | header: ci.yml caller documented as advisory |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/ci.md` | claims aligned with the advisory gate reality |
| `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` | advisory-wiring + staged-hard-gate tests replace the old release-blocking pin |
| `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` | blank-line formatting; same-version dedupe; `|| true` so the missing-version loud fail actually speaks |
| `test/publish_staging_test.dart` | behavioral group executing the stamper (6 tests) |
| `scripts/auto_release.sh` | coalesce age from tagger date |

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproductions before every fix**: E1 race tests under empty `HOME` (thread 1); new guard test against the old blocking ci.yml (thread 2); duplicate-section + formatting + missing-version cases (threads 3/4); tagger-date coalesce test against the old commit-date code (thread 5).
- **Targeted suites (all green)**:
  - `dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` — 127 passed
  - `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` — 89 passed
  - hostile-env re-verification: `HOME=<empty>` E1 group — 7 passed
- **Full suite**: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see final comment status (launched after all edits froze).
- `dart analyze` on the three touched test files: no errors (4 pre-existing info-level `curly_braces` lints, untouched). ci.yml re-parsed as valid YAML.
- Deliberately did **not** run `dart format` on the touched test files: the PR's versions were already format-dirty, so a format pass would add unrelated churn; my edits follow the surrounding style.

Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. {"content":"# Rework — PR #1526 (gh-1522 tag-sourced versions)

All 6 open review threads addressed (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 4 SUGGESTION), the merge conflicts with `main` resolved, and every fix landed TDD-style (RED reproduction → fix → GREEN). The three `no-id` machine records (review summary, gh-807 verdict audit, gh-840 rework-consume) carry no thread/reply targets — the verdict record explicitly says "Do not edit or reply" — so they are covered by this top-level comment instead of threaded replies.

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflicts** (`pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): resolved keeping the gh-1522 `0.0.0-dev` placeholder side (main had bumped versions); resolved and committed as the merge of `origin/main` into `ai/gh-1522` (`1410156bf`).
- **CI root cause** (Quality gate, test-core leg): exactly the BLOCKING thread — the rewritten race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needed an inline git identity. Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.
- Skipped nothing: even the suggestion-level threads got code fixes plus behavioral tests.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. Implemented as a single line: a trailing-backslash continuation proved unreliable inside the generated shim (`-C: command not found`).
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, repo-file changelog gate)** — took the reviewer's option A: the publish gate's repo-file check is now **advisory** (`if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` → `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`); the staged re-measure/trim inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` stays the hard pre-upload gate. Aligned `CHANGELOG.md` header, `docs/ci.md`, `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` header, and rewired the guard test (the old test pinned the release-blocking wiring).
3. **Thread 3 (stamper behavioral tests)** — new group in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` executing the real script against fixture stages: version stamp bytes, Unreleased fold, over-cap oldest-first trim, loud missing-version fail, and the flagged duplicate-curated-section case (fixed in the stamper: a kept section whose header equals the fresh version is dropped).
4. **Thread 4 (blank lines)** — the generated section is now built as `\n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n` over a normalized preamble, matching the repo's hand-curated markdown convention; pinned behaviorally.
5. **Thread 5 (coalesce age)** — `auto_release.sh` reads `%(taggerdate:unix)` via `git for-each-ref` (commit-date fallback for a hypothetical lightweight tag). New divergent-age fixture test: commit 5h old, tag cut now → coalesces.
6. **Thread 6 (stale step name)** — renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)`, matching the binaries-job twin.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` | merge-conflict resolution — keep the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder |

| `scripts/auto_release.sh` | coalesce age from tagger date |

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproductions before every fix**: E1 race tests under empty `HOME` (thread 1); new guard test against the old blocking ci.yml (thread 2); duplicate-section + formatting + missing-version cases (threads 3/4); tagger-date coalesce test against the old commit-date code (thread 5).

```bash
"\$FA_REAL_GIT" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -C "\$FA_RACER" tag -a "\$raced_tag" -m "Release \$raced_tag" origin/main
```

(landed as a single line — a trailing-backslash continuation misbehaved inside the generated shim, so the one-liner is the robust form of the same fix; the seed clone's `git config` indeed does not leak into the racer).

Verified RED→GREEN: with `HOME=<empty dir>` (no global identity, matching the GitHub runner / hostile-env leg) both E1 tests failed exactly as CI showed (`expected 'Tag push raced', got 'Auto-release: pushed v0.1.496'`), and after the fix all tests in the group pass under the same scrubbed environment.

- `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` — the race-hook tag command now pins `-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t` inline.

Fixed — took the first option: the repo-file check in the publish job's `Publish gate` step is now **non-blocking**. An over-cap repo `CHANGELOG.md` emits a `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` as the fix and the release proceeds; the **staged** check inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` (prepend → re-measure → oldest-first trim → last-resort single-section fallback) remains the hard pre-upload gate.

Changes:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` is wrapped in `if ! … ::warning:: … fi` with a comment explaining the repo file is curated-only and not what pub packs.
- `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` — the old test pinning release-blocking wiring (`the guard belongs in the gate step, ahead of staging`) is replaced by two: one pinning the advisory `if !` + `::warning::` + archive-reference wiring, one pinning the staged hard gate ordering (stage step → stamper invocation → `dart pub publish --force`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` header and `docs/ci.md` — both now state the mechanism accurately: the publish job only warns on the repo file; the cap is enforced on the staged file.
- `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` header — caller list updated to mark the ci.yml gate as advisory.

The claim "the 256 KiB cap can no longer block a release" is now true: the uploaded artifact is trimmed under the cap at stage time, and nothing in the release train hard-fails on the repo file's size.

Fixed. The generated section is now built with explicit blank lines matching the repo's hand-curated convention:

```python
preamble = parts[0].rstrip("\n") + "\n"
new = f"\n## {version}\n\n{section.strip()}\n\n"
```

so a stamped file renders:

```markdown
## 1.0.999

- something pending

## 1.0.998
```

Pinned behaviorally in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` (`generated section matches the repo formatting convention`) asserting both the blank after the header and the blank between sections.

Fixed. The coalesce guard now measures the tag object's tagger date:

```bash
tag_ts=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag")
[ -n "$tag_ts" ] || tag_ts=$(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag")  # lightweight-tag fallback
tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - tag_ts ))
```

Pinned with a new divergent-age test in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` (the fixture gained a `commitAgeHours` parameter): a commit sat pending 5h but the tag was cut just now → the run coalesces and pushes nothing. Before the fix this test failed RED (the script measured the 5h-old commit date and pushed v0.1.496); after the fix it passes, and all pre-existing coalesce/race tests stay green.

Fixed. The stale step is renamed to match the binaries-job twin:

```yaml
- name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)
```

It only guards that the committed pubspec still carries the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder — no tag↔pubspec comparison happens there anymore. No test pinned the old name; verified no remaining references to `Verify tag matches pubspec version` anywhere in the tree.

diff --git a/scripts/auto_release.sh b/scripts/auto_release.sh
index 8ad7c8bca..fecba9bd0 100755
--- a/scripts/auto_release.sh
+++ b/scripts/auto_release.sh
@@ -50,7 +50,16 @@ if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
     echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
     exit 0
   fi
-  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag") ))
+  # The 2h window runs from the RELEASE, not from the commit the tag points
+  # at: commits can sit pending on main for hours before the cron/dispatch
+  # cuts the tag (the common catch-up path), and reading the commit date
+  # would let extra releases through exactly when this guard (and the
+  # pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to stop them (PR #1526 thread 5).
+  # Annotated tags carry a tagger date; a lightweight tag (never cut by
+  # this script, but defensive) falls back to the commit date.
+  tag_ts=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag")
+  [ -n "$tag_ts" ] || tag_ts=$(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag")
+  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - tag_ts ))
   if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
     echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
     exit 0
diff --git a/scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh b/scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh
index 15a6edeea..ed504df84 100644
--- a/scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh
+++ b/scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh
@@ -35,7 +35,10 @@ sed -i "s/^version: .*/version: $version/" "$pubspec"
 # invariant's tripwire: a future staging change that drops the pubspec
 # version line, comments it, or carries a second version field fails LOUDLY
 # here instead of shipping a 0.0.0-dev package to pub.dev.
-stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}')
+# `|| true`: a stage whose pubspec dropped the version line must reach the
+# loud invariant message below, not die silently on grep's exit 1 under
+# `set -e` (PR #1526 rework behavioral test).
+stamped=$(grep '^version:' "$pubspec" | awk '{print $2}' || true)
 if [ "$stamped" != "$version" ]; then
   echo "::error::staged pubspec version '$stamped' != release tag version '$version' — refusing to publish (gh-1522 tag↔file invariant)"
   exit 1
@@ -75,14 +78,23 @@ section = os.environ["FA_SECTION"].strip("\n")
 
 text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
 parts = re.split(r"(?=^## )", text, flags=re.M)
-preamble = parts[0]
+preamble = parts[0].rstrip("\n") + "\n"
 versions = [
     s
     for s in parts[1:]
     if s.startswith("## ")
     and not re.match(r"^## Unreleased[ \t]*$", s.split("\n", 1)[0])
+    # PR #1526 rework: the repo file may already carry a curated section
+    # for THIS version (release_notes.sh prefers it) — never keep a
+    # duplicate copy below the generated one.
+    and not re.match(
+        rf"^## {re.escape(version)}[ \t]*$", s.split("\n", 1)[0]
+    )
 ]
-new = f"## {version}\n{section}\n"
+# Blank lines around the header and between sections, matching the repo's
+# hand-curated convention (PR #1526 rework thread 4) — raw markdown must
+# not run sections together: preamble\n + \n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n.
+new = f"\n## {version}\n\n{section.strip()}\n\n"
 size = len((preamble + new).encode("utf-8"))
 kept = []
 for s in versions:  # file order: newest first (the stamp prepends)

{"content":"# Rework — PR #1526 (gh-1522 tag-sourced versions)

All 6 open review threads addressed (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 4 SUGGESTION), the merge conflicts with `main` resolved, and every fix landed TDD-style (RED reproduction → fix → GREEN). The three `no-id` machine records (review summary, gh-807 verdict audit, gh-840 rework-consume) carry no thread/reply targets — the verdict record explicitly says "Do not edit or reply" — so they are covered by this top-level comment instead of threaded replies.

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflicts** (`pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): resolved keeping the gh-1522 `0.0.0-dev` placeholder side (main had bumped versions); all three `git add`ed, `git diff --check` clean.
- **CI root cause** (Quality gate, test-core leg): exactly the BLOCKING thread — the rewritten race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needed an inline git identity. Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.
- Skipped nothing: even the suggestion-level threads got code fixes plus behavioral tests.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. Implemented as a single line: a trailing-backslash continuation proved unreliable inside the generated shim (`-C: command not found`).
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, repo-file changelog gate)** — took the reviewer's option A: the publish gate's repo-file check is now **advisory** (`if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` → `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`); the staged re-measure/trim inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` stays the hard pre-upload gate. Aligned `CHANGELOG.md` header, `docs/ci.md`, `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` header, and rewired the guard test (old test pinned the release-blocking wiring).
3. **Thread 3 (stamper behavioral tests)** — new group in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` executing the real script against fixture stages: version stamp bytes, Unreleased fold, over-cap oldest-first trim, loud missing-version fail, and the flagged duplicate-curated-section case (fixed in the stamper: a kept section whose header equals the fresh version is dropped).
4. **Thread 4 (blank lines)** — the generated section is now built as `\n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n` over a normalized preamble, matching the repo's hand-curated markdown convention; pinned behaviorally.
5. **Thread 5 (coalesce age)** — `auto_release.sh` reads `%(taggerdate:unix)` via `git for-each-ref` (commit-date fallback for a hypothetical lightweight tag). New divergent-age fixture test: commit 5h old, tag cut now → coalesces.
6. **Thread 6 (stale step name)** — renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)`, matching the binaries-job twin.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` | merge-conflict resolution — keep the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder |
| `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` | racer-tag inline identity; `commitAgeHours` fixture param; tagger-date coalesce test |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | advisory repo-file changelog check; stale step renamed |
| `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` | header: ci.yml caller documented as advisory |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/ci.md` | claims aligned with the advisory gate reality |
| `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` | advisory-wiring + staged-hard-gate tests replace the old release-blocking pin |
| `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` | blank-line formatting; same-version dedupe; `|| true` so the missing-version loud fail actually speaks |
| `test/publish_staging_test.dart` | behavioral group executing the stamper (6 tests) |
| `scripts/auto_release.sh` | coalesce age from tagger date |

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproductions before every fix**: E1 race tests under empty `HOME` (thread 1); new guard test against the old blocking ci.yml (thread 2); duplicate-section + formatting + missing-version cases (threads 3/4); tagger-date coalesce test against the old commit-date code (thread 5).
- **Targeted suites (all green)**:
  - `dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` — 127 passed
  - `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` — 89 passed
  - hostile-env re-verification: `HOME=<empty>` E1 group — 7 passed
- **Full suite**: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see final comment status (launched after all edits froze).
- `dart analyze` on the three touched test files: no errors (4 pre-existing info-level `curly_braces` lints, untouched). ci.yml re-parsed as valid YAML.
- Deliberately did **not** run `dart format` on the touched test files: the PR's versions were already format-dirty, so a format pass would add unrelated churn; my edits follow the surrounding style.

{"content":"# Rework — PR #1526 (gh-1522 tag-sourced versions)

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. {"content":"# Rework — PR #1526 (gh-1522 tag-sourced versions)

All 6 open review threads addressed (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 4 SUGGESTION), the merge conflicts with `main` resolved, and every fix landed TDD-style (RED reproduction → fix → GREEN). The three `no-id` machine records (review summary, gh-807 verdict audit, gh-840 rework-consume) carry no thread/reply targets — the verdict record explicitly says "Do not edit or reply" — so they are covered by this top-level comment instead of threaded replies.

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflicts** (`pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): resolved keeping the gh-1522 `0.0.0-dev` placeholder side (main had bumped versions); resolved and committed as the merge of `origin/main` into `ai/gh-1522` (`1410156bf`).
- **CI root cause** (Quality gate, test-core leg): exactly the BLOCKING thread — the rewritten race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needed an inline git identity. Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.
- Skipped nothing: even the suggestion-level threads got code fixes plus behavioral tests.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. Implemented as a single line: a trailing-backslash continuation proved unreliable inside the generated shim (`-C: command not found`).
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, repo-file changelog gate)** — took the reviewer's option A: the publish gate's repo-file check is now **advisory** (`if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` → `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`); the staged re-measure/trim inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` stays the hard pre-upload gate. Aligned `CHANGELOG.md` header, `docs/ci.md`, `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` header, and rewired the guard test (the old test pinned the release-blocking wiring).
3. **Thread 3 (stamper behavioral tests)** — new group in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` executing the real script against fixture stages: version stamp bytes, Unreleased fold, over-cap oldest-first trim, loud missing-version fail, and the flagged duplicate-curated-section case (fixed in the stamper: a kept section whose header equals the fresh version is dropped).
4. **Thread 4 (blank lines)** — the generated section is now built as `\n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n` over a normalized preamble, matching the repo's hand-curated markdown convention; pinned behaviorally.
5. **Thread 5 (coalesce age)** — `auto_release.sh` reads `%(taggerdate:unix)` via `git for-each-ref` (commit-date fallback for a hypothetical lightweight tag). New divergent-age fixture test: commit 5h old, tag cut now → coalesces.
6. **Thread 6 (stale step name)** — renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)`, matching the binaries-job twin.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` | merge-conflict resolution — keep the `0.0.0-dev` placeholder |
| `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` | racer-tag inline identity; `commitAgeHours` fixture param; tagger-date coalesce test |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | advisory repo-file changelog check; stale step renamed |
| `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` | header: ci.yml caller documented as advisory |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/ci.md` | claims aligned with the advisory gate reality |
| `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` | advisory-wiring + staged-hard-gate tests replace the old release-blocking pin |
| `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh` | blank-line formatting; same-version dedupe; `|| true` so the missing-version loud fail actually speaks |
| `test/publish_staging_test.dart` | behavioral group executing the stamper (6 tests) |
| `scripts/auto_release.sh` | coalesce age from tagger date |

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproductions before every fix**: E1 race tests under empty `HOME` (thread 1); new guard test against the old blocking ci.yml (thread 2); duplicate-section + formatting + missing-version cases (threads 3/4); tagger-date coalesce test against the old commit-date code (thread 5).
- **Targeted suites (all green, run before the merge commit)**:
  - `dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/publish_staging_test.dart test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` — 127 passed
  - `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` — 89 passed

- **Full suite**: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` re-launched against the merged tree (`1410156bf`) after the session restart lost the first run — see the follow-up comment for the final count.
- `dart analyze` on the three touched test files: no errors (4 pre-existing info-level `curly_braces` lints, untouched). ci.yml re-parsed as valid YAML.
- Deliberately did **not** run `dart format` on the touched test files: the PR's versions were already format-dirty, so a format pass would add unrelated churn; my edits follow the surrounding style.

{"content":"Fixed. The coalesce guard now measures the tag object's tagger date:

```bash
tag_ts=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag")

tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - tag_ts ))
```

{"content":"# Rework — PR #1526 (gh-1522 tag-sourced versions)

All 6 open review threads addressed (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 4 SUGGESTION), the merge conflicts with `main` resolved, and every fix landed TDD-style (RED reproduction → fix → GREEN). The three `no-id` machine records (review summary, gh-807 verdict audit, gh-840 rework-consume) carry no thread/reply targets — the verdict record explicitly says "Do not edit or reply" — so they are covered by this top-level comment instead of threaded replies.

## Issues/Notes

- **Merge conflicts** (`pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): resolved keeping the gh-1522 `0.0.0-dev` placeholder side (main had bumped versions); resolved and committed as the merge of `origin/main` into `ai/gh-1522` (`1410156bf`).
- **CI root cause** (Quality gate, test-core leg): exactly the BLOCKING thread — the rewritten race hook's `git tag -a` in the racer clone needed an inline git identity. Reproduced locally with an empty `HOME` (no global identity): both E1 tests failed precisely as on the runner; fixed and re-verified under the same scrubbed environment.
- While adding the requested stamper behavioral tests, the missing-version-line case exposed a real gap: `set -e` killed the stamper on grep's exit 1 *before* its loud invariant message — now guarded with `|| true` so the descriptive `::error::` fires.
- Skipped nothing: even the suggestion-level threads got code fixes plus behavioral tests.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, CI red)** — restored the inline identity (`-c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t`) on the racer's annotated-tag command in the `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` race hook, matching the retired pre-gh-1522 pattern. Implemented as a single line: a trailing-backslash continuation proved unreliable inside the generated shim (`-C: command not found`).
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, repo-file changelog gate)** — took the reviewer's option A: the publish gate's repo-file check is now **advisory** (`if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md` → `::warning::` naming `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`); the staged re-measure/trim inside `stamp_staged_release.sh` stays the hard pre-upload gate. Aligned `CHANGELOG.md` header, `docs/ci.md`, `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` header, and rewired the guard test (the old test pinned the release-blocking wiring).
3. **Thread 3 (stamper behavioral tests)** — new group in `test/publish_staging_test.dart` executing the real script against fixture stages: version stamp bytes, Unreleased fold, over-cap oldest-first trim, loud missing-version fail, and the flagged duplicate-curated-section case (fixed in the stamper: a kept section whose header equals the fresh version is dropped).
4. **Thread 4 (blank lines)** — the generated section is now built as `\n## <version>\n\n<body>\n\n` over a normalized preamble, matching the repo's hand-curated markdown convention; pinned behaviorally.
5. **Thread 5 (coalesce age)** — `auto_release.sh` reads `%(taggerdate:unix)` via `git for-each-ref` (commit-date fallback for a hypothetical lightweight tag). New divergent-age fixture test: commit 5h old, tag cut now → coalesces.
6. **Thread 6 (stale step name)** — renamed to `Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)`, matching the binaries-job twin.

|---|---|

| `test/publish_staging_test.dart` | behavioral group executing the stamper (6 tests) |
| `scripts/auto_release.sh` | coalesce age from tagger date |

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproductions before every fix**: E1 race tests under empty `HOME` (thread 1); new guard test against the old blocking ci.yml (thread 2); duplicate-section + formatting + missing-version cases (threads 3/4); tagger-date coalesce test against the old commit-date code (thread 5).
